31/* @brief Base class for all bots components (controllers, sensors, actuators).
32 * Provides common state: the associated actor's stale-safe identity, a validity flag, and the
33 * Destroy pattern. The validity flag is set to false by RoboticsContext before deletion, allowing
34 * dangling-pointer detection alongside generational handles.
35 *
36 * The associated actor is NOT cached as a raw pointer. Its stale-safe identity (@ref ActorHandle /
37 * @ref SceneHandle / owning @ref Context) is retained and @ref GetActor resolves the live
38 * @ref Actor* on demand, yielding nullptr once the owning scene (or the actor) has been destroyed.
39 * A component that outlives its mochi Scene (e.g. the Scene was destroyed before the
40 * RoboticsContext) therefore never dereferences a dangling Actor* — callers check @ref GetActor for
41 * null. This assumes the mochi @ref Context outlives the RoboticsContext — the outermost lifetime
42 * in the mochi ownership graph. */
43class MOCHI_API ComponentBase {
44 public:
45 ComponentBase(ComponentBase const&) = delete;
46 ComponentBase& operator=(ComponentBase const&) = delete;
47 ComponentBase(ComponentBase&&) = delete;
48 ComponentBase& operator=(ComponentBase&&) = delete;
49
50 /* @brief Whether this component remains usable. Returns false after its owning
51 * @ref RoboticsContext destroys it.
52 * @return True while the component is live. */
53 [[nodiscard]] bool IsValid() const {
54 return _isValid;
55 }
56 /* @brief Resolve the live @ref Actor* this component is bound to, or nullptr if it was
57 * constructed without an actor or its owning scene/actor has since been destroyed. Resolved on
58 * demand from the stale-safe handle each call (an O(1) scene lookup), so it is always current and
59 * never returns a dangling pointer — dereference only after a null check.
60 * @return Live associated actor, or nullptr if none is available. */
61 [[nodiscard]] Actor* GetActor() const;
62
63 /* @brief The bot this component was created on, or nullptr if it was created directly on an actor
64 * (not via a bot) — e.g. a scene-level sensor or a controller built on a raw articulation. Used
65 * to scope FindByName / FindByType to a single bot and to drive DestroyBot's component cascade.
66 * Borrowed: the owning bot is owned by the RoboticsContext, which destroys a bot's components
67 * before the bot itself, so this never dangles. Held as a raw pointer (not a handle) because a
68 * bot is not scene-owned, so the stale-safety the actor handles provide is unnecessary here.
69 * @return Owning bot, or nullptr if this component has no owning bot. */
70 [[nodiscard]] Bot* GetOwningBot() const {
71 return _owningBot;
72 }
73
74 /* @brief This component's instance name, or empty if it was created without one. Names are NOT
75 * required to be unique, so name-based lookups (FindByName) may return multiple matches.
76 * @return Instance name; empty if unnamed. */
77 [[nodiscard]] std::string_view GetName() const {
78 return {_name.c_str(), _name.size()};
79 }
80
81 /* @brief This component's registered type name (e.g. "BASIC_OSC_PD", "SENSOR_CAMERA"), reported
82 * polymorphically. Declared here so controllers, sensors, and actuators can be searched by type
83 * uniformly (FindByType); each component kind implements it.
84 * @return Registered component type name. */
85 [[nodiscard]] virtual std::string_view GetTypeName() const = 0;
86
87 /* @brief Reset internal state without destroying the component.
88 * Parameters are preserved. Use between episodes to clear stale state
89 * (e.g., derivative tracking, timing diagnostics). */
90 virtual void Reset() = 0;
91
92 /* @brief Destroy a component created by a static Create function.
93 * Sets the validity flag to false before deletion.
94 * @param component Pointer to the component to destroy. May be nullptr (no-op).
95 * Only callable by RoboticsContext — destroy via RoboticsContext methods. */
96 static void Destroy(ComponentBase* component);
97
98 protected:
99 /* @brief Capture @p actor's stale-safe identity (handle, owning scene handle, and owning context)
100 * so the live actor can be resolved on demand via @ref GetActor. A null @p actor is permitted
101 * (actor-less components such as fusion sensors or real-robot controllers). */
102 explicit ComponentBase(Actor* actor);
103
104 /* @brief Mark this component as invalid. Called by RoboticsContext before deletion. */
105 void SetInvalid() {
106 _isValid = false;
107 }
108
109 /* @brief The owning mochi @ref Context, or nullptr if constructed without an actor. The context
110 * is the outermost lifetime in the mochi ownership graph, so (under the standing contract that it
111 * outlives the RoboticsContext) this raw pointer stays valid for the component's whole life.
112 * Useful in destructors to release context-owned resources even after the actor/scene are gone.
113 */
114 [[nodiscard]] Context* GetContext() const {
115 return _context;
116 }
117
118 /* @brief Resolve the owning mochi @ref Scene from its stale-safe handle, or nullptr if this
119 * component was constructed without an actor or its owning scene has since been destroyed. Prefer
120 * this over caching a raw @ref Scene*: a component that outlives its scene resolves to nullptr
121 * (so callers can bail) instead of dereferencing a dangling pointer. */
122 [[nodiscard]] Scene* GetScene() const;
123
124 // NOLINTNEXTLINE(cppcoreguidelines-virtual-class-destructor)
125 virtual ~ComponentBase();
126
127 private:
128 friend class RoboticsContext;
129
130 /* @brief Record the bot this component was created on. Called by RoboticsContext at creation
131 * time; left null for components created directly on an actor. */
132 void SetOwningBot(Bot* bot) {
133 _owningBot = bot;
134 }
135
136 /* @brief Set this component's instance name. Called by RoboticsContext at creation time. Copies
137 * @p name into an owned, null-terminated string (the view need not outlive the call). */
138 void SetName(std::string_view name) {
139 _name = DynamicString(std::string(name).c_str());
140 }
141
142 /* Stale-safe identity of the associated actor and its owning scene, plus the owning context used
143 * to resolve them. Captured from the actor at construction; the handles stay meaningful after the
144 * actor/scene are destroyed (resolution then yields nullptr). */
145 ActorHandle _actorHandle;
146 SceneHandle _sceneHandle;
147 Context* _context = nullptr;
148 /* The bot this component was created on (see GetOwningBot); null for actor-scoped components. */
149 Bot* _owningBot = nullptr;
150 /* This component's instance name (see GetName); empty when created without one. */
151 DynamicString _name;
152 bool _isValid = true;
153};
